source_refs.note: Exercise 13.1, Question 8 (book page 248, PDF 253); answer key PDF 310-311.

blocks.prompt: 8 Find the gradient of the curve \(f(x) = 3x^2 + 2x\) at \(x = 1\).
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein sirf gradient (curve ki dhalaan) poocha gaya hai, line ki equation nahi.
Curve ki gradient kisi point par wahan tangent ki slope hoti hai, yani \(f'(1)\).
Plan: \(f'(x)\) definition se, phir \(x = 1\) rakhenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(f(x) = 3x^2 + 2x\), \(x = 1\).
Find karna hai: gradient \(f'(1)\).
Tareeqa: definition (first principles / ab-initio, yani bilkul shuru se) se derivative: \(f'(x) = \lim_{\delta x \to 0} \frac{f(x + \delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x}\). Chaar steps yaad rakhein: (I) \(f(x + \delta x)\) likhein; (II) us mein se \(f(x)\) minus karein; (III) \(\delta x\) se divide karein; (IV) \(\delta x \to 0\) ka limit lein. Yeh tareeqa is liye ke Exercise 13.1 mein sawal khud 'by definition' maangta hai, aur power rule waghera abhi Section 13.6 mein aaenge; is liye shortcut nahi, poora limit ka safar dikhana hai.

Step I aur II: \(f(x + \delta x) - f(x)\)
\[f(x + \delta x) = 3(x + \delta x)^2 + 2(x + \delta x)\]
\[= 3x^2 + 6x\,\delta x + 3(\delta x)^2 + 2x + 2\,\delta x\]
\[f(x + \delta x) - f(x) = 6x\,\delta x + 3(\delta x)^2 + 2\,\delta x\]
Kyun: \(x\) ki jagah \(x + \delta x\) rakha, brackets khole, phir \(f(x)\) minus kiya; \(3x^2\) aur \(2x\) cancel ho gaye.

Step III aur IV: divide aur limit
\[\dfrac{f(x + \delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x} = 6x + 3\,\delta x + 2\]
\[f'(x) = 6x + 2\]
Kyun: \(\delta x\) cancel kiya (abhi woh zero nahi), phir \(\delta x = 0\) rakha.

\(x = 1\) par gradient
\[f'(1) = 6(1) + 2 = 8\]
Kyun: \(f'(x)\) mein \(x = 1\) rakha. Dhyan dein: \(f(1) = 5\) curve ki height hai, gradient nahi. Gradient derivative se aati hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{f(1.01) - f(1)}{0.01} = \dfrac{5.0803 - 5}{0.01} = 8.03 \approx 8 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(x = 1\) se thora sa aage ki average slope \(8.03\) aayi, jo \(8\) ke bohat qareeb hai. Interval aur chhota karein to yeh \(8\) ke aur qareeb hoti jayegi.
